# Outline and Contour Generation

Also called: Outline Generation, Contour Rendering, Edge Highlighting

## Overview
Outline and Contour Generation is a family of non-photorealistic volume rendering techniques that enhance perceptual clarity by explicitly rendering line primitives to demarcate object boundaries, silhouettes, and feature edges [G]. Unlike photorealistic shading which relies on illumination models to suggest form, these methods generate high-contrast strokes that define shape and structure regardless of lighting conditions [S1, unofficial]. What sets this family apart from its siblings is the specific focus on *boundary definition* through line-based abstraction, distinguishing it from [Line Illustration Detection](772-line-illustration-detection.md) (which focuses on artistic stroke style), [Face-based volume rendering with edge highlights](2453-face-based-volume-rendering-with-edge-highlights.md) (which highlights edges on rendered surfaces), and [LOG-based Silhouette Detection](6322-log-based-silhouette-detection.md) (which uses Laplacian of Gaussian filtering specifically).

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental goal of enhancing perceptual clarity through non-photorealistic edge representation [G]. Common mechanisms include:
1. **Edge Detection:** Identifying boundaries based on local volumetric properties (gradients, Laplacian of Gaussian) or image-space properties (depth, normal discontinuities) [S2].
2. **Line Rendering:** Converting detected edges into line primitives (strips, segments) or stylized strokes [S2].

## Subtopics

### [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md)
Object Contour NPR generates view-dependent line primitives that demarcate areas where an object's surface turns away from the viewer, conveying shape through boundary emphasis. Unlike hatches, which are often pre-rendered to texture buffers, these contours are traced and rendered directly to the screen in real-time. It differs from direct volume rendering by relying solely on gradient magnitude and viewing angle rather than voxel intensity values, allowing for faster parameter tuning. See [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md).

### [Image Space Outline Generation](788-image-space-outline-generation.md)
Image Space Outline Generation is a post-processing technique that renders non-photorealistic outlines by detecting discontinuities in screen-space depth or normal buffers. It solves the problem of defining object boundaries in volume rendering without the computational overhead of analytical geometry processing. Unlike sibling methods that compute contours from volumetric gradients or topological features, this method relies on simple pixel-wise comparisons of existing rasterization buffers, making it significantly faster and easier to implement. See [Image Space Outline Generation](788-image-space-outline-generation.md).

### [Lasso Contour Rendering](1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md)
Lasso Contour Rendering is an interactive non-photorealistic volume rendering technique that allows users to manually define regions of interest using a free-form selection tool to generate contour overlays [G]. It solves the problem of isolating complex volumetric structures that lack sharp boundaries by enabling user-driven contour generation [G]. It differs from siblings like [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md) by relying on explicit user interaction to define the region of interest rather than automatic geometric or scalar-based detection [G]. See [Lasso Contour Rendering](1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md).

### [Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md)
Curvature-Controlled Style Contours is a volume rendering technique that regulates contour thickness based on the normal curvature along the view direction to prevent the uncontrolled variation in thickness inherent in standard dot-product silhouette methods. While standard methods ($v \cdot n \approx 0$) produce contours that are too thick on flat surfaces and too thin on fine structures, this method uses curvature to maintain consistent visual weight across varying surface geometries. It builds on [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by integrating curvature-aware edge detection with style transfer functions. See [Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md).

### [Silhouette Rendering](7959-silhouette-rendering.md)
Silhouette rendering is an object-space line rendering technique that extracts significant edges (silhouettes and feature lines) from geometry, assembles them into strokes, and renders them with stylization to enhance perceptual clarity. It solves the problem of discriminating object classes or indicating context objects (e.g., bones) by rendering "interesting" features with silhouettes while leaving others without. Unlike image-space methods, it operates on pre-extracted geometric primitives, allowing for independent stylization and combination with surface or volume rendering. See [Silhouette Rendering](7959-silhouette-rendering.md).

### [Topological Landscape](8481-topological-landscape.md)
Topological Landscape is a visualization technique that maps the connectivity of a scalar field’s level sets onto a 3D terrain model using the contour tree. It solves the problem of interpreting complex topological relationships (merges and splits of contours) by leveraging human intuition for reading physical terrain. It sets itself apart from standard contour rendering by transforming abstract graph nodes into a spatial height map where peaks and valleys explicitly encode topological events, differing from [Contour Tree](9312-contour-tree.md) by providing a geometric metaphor rather than just a hierarchical graph structure. See [Topological Landscape](8481-topological-landscape.md).

### [Boundary Enhancement Volume Style](10863-boundary-enhancement-volume-style.md)
Boundary Enhancement Volume Style is a non-photorealistic rendering technique designed to highlight feature boundaries within volumetric data while simultaneously reducing visual noise. It operates by detecting local intensity gradients or structural discontinuities to generate edge-like highlights, distinct from standard photorealistic shading which focuses on surface illumination. Unlike sibling methods such as [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md) which may rely on geometric mesh extraction, this method operates directly in the volume space to preserve internal structure visibility while emphasizing edges. See [Boundary Enhancement Volume Style](10863-boundary-enhancement-volume-style.md).

### [Suggestive Contour Extraction](13101-suggestive-contour-extraction.md)
Suggestive contour extraction identifies surface locations where radial curvature is zero but increasing towards the viewer, complementing standard object contours to enhance shape perception in non-photorealistic volume rendering. Unlike standard contours which mark visible boundaries, suggestive contours reveal hidden or occluded geometry, such as the rims of indentations, by detecting where the surface is about to curve towards the camera. See [Suggestive Contour Extraction](13101-suggestive-contour-extraction.md).

### [Bounding Wall Contour Overlay](16354-bounding-wall-contour-overlay.md)
Bounding Wall Contour Overlay is a non-photorealistic visualization technique that displays line contours of a reference scalar field on the vertical bounding walls of a 3D volume. It solves the problem of providing spatial context for deformed interfaces (such as billows or panels) without occluding the primary data or introducing visual clutter. Unlike sibling methods that render edges within the volume or in image space, this method projects 2D contour lines onto the 3D scene's boundary planes, ensuring the annotations are read as context rather than competing data surfaces. See [Bounding Wall Contour Overlay](16354-bounding-wall-contour-overlay.md).

#### Ghosted Views with Contours
Ghosted Views with Contours is a technique where the visual representation of context objects is reduced to contours in areas of occlusion to reveal pre-segmented internal structures [S1, unofficial]. For example, in medical visualization, the body (context) may be rendered as contours behind a segmented internal organ (interesting structure) to provide spatial context without obscuring the target [S1, unofficial]. See [Ghosted Views with Contours](ghosted-views-with-contours.md) for implementation details.

#### 2D Stroke to 3D Line Picking
2D Stroke to 3D Line Picking is a method that locates the intended location of a 2D stroke in 3D space by finding the 3D line that is a projection of the 2D stroke and fits contours in the data best (dot product of normal vector of extruded stroke and gradient in data) [S2]. It only works at contours of objects and segments objects whose contour best fits the stroke, which may not be the most visible objects, whereas WYSIWYP is applicable to any position in the rendering [S2]. See [2D Stroke to 3D Line Picking](2d-stroke-to-3d-line-picking.md) for implementation details.

## Background
The concept of using outlines to enhance shape perception in volume rendering has roots in non-photorealistic rendering (NPR) techniques adapted for scientific visualization. Early work focused on object-space contour generation, such as the VolumeFlies framework, which traced contours directly from volumetric data [S1, unofficial]. The field expanded to include image-space methods for efficiency and topological methods for structural understanding [S1, unofficial]. The integration of curvature control and suggestive contours addressed limitations in standard silhouette methods regarding thickness variation and hidden geometry [S1, unofficial]. The family is widely used in medical visualization (e.g., CT angiography, organ segmentation) and scientific data analysis to clarify complex spatial relationships [S1, unofficial].
